Senzo Meyiwa Suspect

By: Ntokozo Miya | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Zamo Mbatha - THE FIRST, AND FORGOTTEN, SENZO MEYIWA MURDER SUSPECT - says his life has never been the same since he was accused of killing soccer star, Senzo Meyiwa. He shares what the last ten years

Unique Selling Point:
Using the 2014 Carte Blanche insert on Senzo Meyiwa's murder as a launchpad, we recount the experience of the first suspect arrested for the crime, and what he says has been a life-long negative impact on his life.

Summary:
In 2014, a 26-year-old from Vosloorus finally decided to get his life together after being unable to further his education and get stable employment. Up until late that year, he did odd jobs on occasion and had little ambition, having accepted his dire circumstances. By then he had a girlfriend who motivated to try to turn his life around by finding a job. He eventually did find a job, at a construction site.
It being a construction, he wasn't making much money so he continued his small side hustles including washing cars, occasional painting jobs – his favorite was washing the car of a soccer star because the player tipped generously and that money would keep him going for two or three weeks.
On the 26th of October 2014, that soccer star was gunned down at the home of his girlfriend, not far from where he lives.
The soccer star was Senzo Meyiwa, his girlfriend, Kelly Khumalo. The young man who cleaned Senzo's car was Zamo Mbatha, who lived a short walk from the Khumalo home. He was shocked and saddened by the death of the national soccer hero... not knowing that just 3 days later, he would be arrested and presented to the public as the killer.
Considering his background of poverty and financial struggle, he was terrified that he could very little to protect himself legally and in the media. But, miraculously to him, after being detained for two weeks, he was released after the court decided that there was a lack of evidence linking him to the case. But his life had already been destroyed as members of his own community and soccer fans still thought that he wouldn't have been implicated in the first place if he wasn't guilty.
During one traumatic incident while he was in jail, community members attempted to burn his shack, with his girlfriend inside.
Just last month in July, Zamo's lawsuit against the police minister was indefinitely postponed, yet again in the nearly 10 years since he launched it.

Further information:
Zamo lays the foundation on which we examine he case against him and his ongoing legal battle. We also analyze the latest developments in the case and explore the possibility of this trial being able to finally put to rest the matter of #JusticeForSenzoMeyiwa.

Extra Budget Items:
Waiting on SABC to find Zamo Mbatha archives and provide quote.

Script:


THE FIRST SUSPECT

GRAPHIC / 2014

1 VO – A South African football icon and captain of the Bafana Bafana team, hailed as one of Africa's top goalkeepers.

This was Senzo Meyiwa.

SENZO MEYIWA – CB 2014: I used to joke a lot at training but now, I hold my jokes...

2 VO – On a rainy day in October 2014 – the 27-year-old plays his last match.

UPS MATCH

3 VO – The very next day, as he visits his girlfriend in Vosloorus, tragedy strikes.

Senzo is fatally shot in an apparent home invasion.

BONGANI BINGWA – CB STUDIO: [00:00:00.17] - … “Our national football captain, Senzo Meyiwa, was gunned down at the home of his girlfriend's mother on the East Rand.

4 VO – The nation mourns – questions swirling around events at the crime scene, the home of musician Kelly Khumalo’s mother where seven people converged: the musician, her mother and sister, their partners and close friends.

PAUSE

It's said that one intruder carries a gun and demands money and cell phones and in a scruffle - Senzo is shot in the chest.

VIZ: colour image from the funeral

5 VO – Under intense public pressure, police made a swift arrest.

VIZ: house? Cops? What’s on the old CB story that we can use?

6 VO – The police’s prime suspect lives down the street.
His girlfriend Celiwe Ndima sees the police arrive at their home.
CELIWE NDIMA – ZAMO'S GIRLFRIEND: 03:02 Yes. I was in the house and three police officers arrived. These police officers had Zamo’s picture. They showed me the picture and asked if I knew the person. I said yes I know him, he stays in this house. 03:17
7 VO – Her boyfriend is called Zamokuhle Mbatha – he’s busy at the nearby carwash.
CELIWE NDIMA – ZAMO'S GIRLFRIEND: There were eight cars and four vans. - 06:04 I showed them where Zamo was sitting. … - 04:03 04:58 - One of them said, “It's really him, he’ll tell the truth.” They got there and grabbed him by his shorts, lifted him, and left with him. - 04:03
8 VO – It emerges that witness at the crime scene has pointed out Zamo.
ZAMOKUHLE MBATHA: 13:42 That’s how I was picked out. I was arrested and told thatI was identified by two people who were in the house. They likened me to that person. They were saying it was me actually. I was handcuffed and taken to the police station for fingerprinting.
9 VO – It becomes the longest days of Zamo’s life as he’s hauled in for questioning and an identity parade.

ZAMOKUHLE MBATHA: I was arrested after being identified by two people who were in the house.

10 VO – With great fanfare police brief the press that they’ve got a man responsible for Senzo's murder.

VINESH MONOO – SAPS HEAD OF DETECTIVES – EWN: “We are sure that the person that we have now charged is one of the suspects.”

11 VO – But there’s a glaring problem: For the fateful night, Zamo has an alibi. Celiwe. They were sound asleep at home they say.

Within days it becomes clear that the police can’t make their case against Zamo stick - two weeks later, they release him.

JUDGE DANIEL THULARE – EWN: There is no sufficient evidential material ... This court orders the immediate release of the accused.

12 VO – For six years the police investigation seems to stall.

It’s only in 2020 that they claim to have linked a suspect to the firearm that killed Meyiwa.

It’s six years of pure hell for Zamo. He loses his job and sinks into depression.

PAUSE

LINK – FX3_9885 - He was the first suspect in the murder of Senzo Meyiwa. It's nearly ten years later and Zamokuhle Mbatha recalls the most terrifying two weeks that changed his life forever.

13 VO – Zamo knew the Khumalos.. and used to see the famous footballer around.

ZAMOKUHLE MBATHA: He liked people and was a good guy. - 00:07:11:15
00:05:46:10 - I used to work at the car wash. He would bring his car to get cleaned. I was very active at the car wash.

14 VO – So why would someone inside the house, at the crime scene, point to him?

ZAMOKUHLE MBATHA: They took me to the police station. They showed me an identikit picture of someone with dreadlocks.

15 VO – the picture appeared everywhere.

ZAMOKUHLE MBATHA: It was in the morning newspaper and I had also seen it.

MAC – 00:12:41:00 – Did you think this person looks like you and might have similar features?

ZAMOKUHLE MBATHA: 00:11:57:15 – The dreads were the only similarity because they were the same length at the time.

VISUAL CLIMAX/PUNCHLINE… VIZ: make the photo versus identikit comparison the big reveal

MAC – 13:13 - … Are you at some point thinking that, ‘The Khumalo's know me, they should be telling these people that it’s not me, I’m not that person.’

ZAMOKUHLE MBATHA: 14:09 - That’s what I kept saying. I was at their house on the Monday, with the rest of the community. They could have pointed me out then if I was the intruder.

BREATHER

16 VO – After his arrest is announced – hurt and angry community members storm Zamo’s home, demanding answers.

CELIWE NDIMA – ZAMO'S GIRLFRIEND: 06:49 - People who wanted to burn the house were not inside the yard, they were outside. … Some said, “This girl knows something because he's her boyfriend. If we kill her or burn this shack, everything will end.”

17 VO – Neighbours who know the couple manage to disperse the crowd.

BREATHER

18 VO – When Zamo is released two weeks later, it’s without the big press conference.

He’s unable to shift the stigma and suspicion.

ZAMOKUHLE MBATHA: 21:14 – I was scared I might be killed because I heard rumours that people wanted me to be taken to the stadium, so they could finish me off. - 21:29

19 VO – Zamo has been struggling to make ends meet.

ZAMOKUHLE MBATHA: My girlfriend, is the one who tries to gets temporary work as a domestic and things like that. At home I have a brother I can lean on when I need help.

MAC LINK – FX3_9888 - You know, I can almost feel and understand Zamo's anger and frustration, not only at the community but the police, but most of all at the people that were in the house who knew him, who saw him everyday, and they know that he was not the person that pulled that trigger, and ten years later, their lives moved on and they carried on, and to this day, his life is standing still.

2020

20 VO – It would take eight years for Meyiwa’s high-profile trial to get underway, raising allegations of coverups along the way.

It's only in 2020 that police parade another five suspects.

POLICE MINISTER BHEKI CELE – GOVERNMENTZA: We have a watertight case against all five suspects.


2023

21 VO – By 2023 after numerous delays, Judge Tshifhiwa Maumela is suspended for his failure to deliver judgements - within deadline - in other cases.

UPS:

The trial restarts before retired Judge Ratha Mokgoatlheng.

Legal analyst Thabo Masombuka hopes this will finally bring closure and justice.

THABO MASOMBUKA – LEGAL ANALYST: We saw a little bit of a sense of urgency in the manner in which the judge conducts the conveyance of evidence. He's a bit interfering, but interfering to ensure that the procedure is followed to the 't', curtailing unnecessary lines of questioning, but also in ensuring that there is an expeditious trial.

22 VO – And figuring out who the infamous dreadlocked man is remains key to the trial.

UPS COURT 31 JULY 2023: the person who is depicted in the photo there has got dreadlocks…has got a particular hairstyle...

Zamo is trying to fight back... reportedly suing the police for close to twenty million rands.

BREATHER

MAC LINK LINK - FX6_5128 – 00:00:15:19 – Over the past ten years, Zamo's life has basically stood still, and during this period he's been trying to sue the state but is there ever an amount of compensation that will ever be enough to get his ten years back.

23 VO – Last year alone police received nearly thirteen thousand claims for unlawful arrests – that’s over twelve billion rands.

THABO MASOMBUKA – LEGAL ANALYST: Police irresponsibility and recklessness in this country. It's not going to be resolved until courts zoom into the personal pension funds of these police officers.

ZAMOKUHLE MBATHA: Tradition dictates that when you’re falsely accused and it turns out that you’re innocent

MAC – They must pay damages.

ZAMOKUHLE MBATHA: They have to pay damages.

24 VO – Shockingly, police haven't let Zamo off the hook completely - as the case continues.
POLICE COMMISSIONER GEN. KHEHLA SITHOLE - GOVERNMENTZA – YOUTUBE: Until the final scope of the investigation is done, we will then know whether any suspect who might have been arrested before, did we make a mistake. The investigation still continues.

25 VO – with Zamo’s lawsuit pending, the police and witnesses can't comment.

To this day he's struggling to make peace.

ZAMOKUHLE MBATHA: MAC - 28:31 - And still to this day, no apology from the Khumalo’s, nothing from the police. No one has ever apologised.

UPS FROM COURT 28 July: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9WFr5hF4Y2U&t=2568s

01 39 49 JUDGE: FROM MY UNDERSTANDING, the linkage – when does it start?

26 VO – As the murder trial finally makes progress – will it reveal who killed Senzo Meyiwa – and why?

VIZ: 51 19 LAASTE DAG VAN TRIAL VANDAG : https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s7ocKRy30rY

PROMO 2

VO – When soccer star Senzo Meyiwa was shot and killed - police arrested the wrong man

ZAMO – I was arrested after being identified by two people who were in the house.

VO – Ostracised by his community - his life was never the same.

ZAMO – I was scared that I may be killed. I heard rumours that people wanted me to be taken to the stadium, so they could finish me off.



PROMO 3

VO Arrested and paraded in court, he was the first suspect in Senzo Meyiwa’s murder

ZAMO - They said I was connected to the incident, I went into the house and shot him.

VO – But they got it wrong…

JUDGE DANIEL THULARE - “There is no sufficient evidential material ... This court orders the immediate release of the accused.”

VO – A decade later, he’s demanding justice and compensation for his wrongful arrest.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Using the 2014 Carte Blanche insert on Senzo Meyiwa's murder as a launchpad, we recount the experience of the first suspect arrested for the crime, and what he says has been a life-long negative impact on his life.
metadata.Summary: In 2014, a 26-year-old from Vosloorus finally decided to get his life together after being unable to further his education and get stable employment. Up until late that year, he did odd jobs on occasion and had little ambition, having accepted his dire circumstances. By then he had a girlfriend who motivated to try to turn his life around by finding a job. He eventually did find a job, at a construction site. It being a construction, he wasn't making much money so he continued his small side hustles including washing cars, occasional painting jobs – his favorite was washing the car of a soccer star because the player tipped generously and that money would keep him going for two or three weeks. On the 26th of October 2014, that soccer star was gunned down at the home of his girlfriend, not far from where he lives. The soccer star was Senzo Meyiwa, his girlfriend, Kelly Khumalo. The young man who cleaned Senzo's car was Zamo Mbatha, who lived a short walk from the Khumalo home. He was shocked and saddened by the death of the national soccer hero... not knowing that just 3 days later, he would be arrested and presented to the public as the killer. Considering his background of poverty and financial struggle, he was terrified that he could very little to protect himself legally and in the media. But, miraculously to him, after being detained for two weeks, he was released after the court decided that there was a lack of evidence linking him to the case. But his life had already been destroyed as members of his own community and soccer fans still thought that he wouldn't have been implicated in the first place if he wasn't guilty. During one traumatic incident while he was in jail, community members attempted to burn his shack, with his girlfriend inside. Just last month in July, Zamo's lawsuit against the police minister was indefinitely postponed, yet again in the nearly 10 years since he launched it.
metadata.Further information: Zamo lays the foundation on which we examine he case against him and his ongoing legal battle. We also analyze the latest developments in the case and explore the possibility of this trial being able to finally put to rest the matter of #JusticeForSenzoMeyiwa.
